clue.text: Some acres specifically for salad plant

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A farmer sets aside a few acres expressly to grow salad greens.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'for', but 'for' is only the link joining wordplay to definition; 'salad plant' alone defines. 'Some' asks for a run of letters inside 'acres specifically'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cress is a peppery leafy green eaten raw in salads and sandwiches.

clue.text: Artist in front colours in the sky

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword staple for an artist
the bow is the front end of a ship

explanation.surface: A painter stands before a vivid sky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a container signal but just gives its own letters; 'front' is the forward end of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainbow is the arc of spectral bands seen when sunlight passes through rain.

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A woman lends half-hearted support to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backs' looks like a reversal signal, but the letters are read forwards from 'she backs'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Queen of Sheba is the biblical ruler who visited Solomon, so the name stands for a queen.

clue.text: Actor's whispered remark from a team

parts.note: a side is a team in sport, as in a football side

explanation.surface: A stage player mutters something to a group of teammates.
explanation.definitionFit: On stage, a line spoken to the audience that other characters supposedly cannot hear is this kind of remark.

explanation.surface: Discs are played at the sports event.
explanation.definitionFit: Singles are records with one main track; in tennis it also names a one-against-one contest.

parts.note: aft means at or towards the rear, as on a ship

explanation.surface: A physician lurks behind a drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough first version of a picture or document is a preliminary outline, a sketch.

clue.text: Ointment takes up most of the tray

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter, so the word for tray loses its end

parts.note: a salver is a flat serving tray

explanation.surface: A tube of cream hogs nearly all the space on a tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing balm applied to skin or wounds is a medicinal cream.

explanation.surface: Something occurring turns out to be a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A FOOT, the word is an appendage; whole, it means under way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something under way or in progress is said to be going on; a foot is a body extremity.

clue.text: Quietly called to report small accident

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
rang means telephoned, called someone

explanation.surface: Someone phones in softly to own up to a minor mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: PRANG is British slang for a minor collision, especially a car bump.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a minor crash or bump, typically involving a car.

indicators.note: preceded by puts the following piece in front of the insects

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects

explanation.surface: Some bugs come behind a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is a girl's name, as in Lewis Carroll's heroine.

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the letters of the thug word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thug vandalises fairground attractions.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling fair offering stalls, side attractions and mechanical amusements.

clue.text: Bravo! It becomes fluctuation of pitch

indicators.note: becomes means turns into something else, so the letters of the two words are recast

explanation.surface: An audience cheer turns into a wobble in a singer's voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrato is a rapid regular wavering of a musical note, used by singers and string players.

clue.text: It was the talk of Rome

definitions.text: It was the talk of Rome

parts.words: It was the talk of Rome
parts.note: reads like gossip everyone in the city was discussing, but means the language spoken by Romans

explanation.surface: Something was the scandal that all of Rome gossiped about.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Romans spoke Latin, so it was literally their speech.

indicators.note: dismisses means sends away, so the following little word is removed from the port

parts.note: Antwerp is a major port city in Belgium

explanation.surface: A Belgian harbour city sacks a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or annoying person, a fool.

clue.text: Understood about university having yen for mischief

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word's letters go round the abbreviation

parts.note: roger is the radio reply meaning message received and understood
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A student grasped that campus life included a craving for pranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Roguery is rascally, playful misbehaviour or dishonest conduct.

clue.text: You and I take a long time to get employment

parts.note: you and I together are us
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Two people wait ages before landing a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means the act of using something, its use or employment.

parts.note: suggests a bloom caught by frost, but a flower here is something that flows, and this one is made of ice

explanation.surface: A bloom has been killed by frost.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacier is a slow-moving river of ice, so it is a thing that flows while frozen.

indicators.note: included says the answer sits inside the words before it

explanation.surface: A folk song turns out to contain explicit content after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' seems to ask for a last letter, but it is just part of the text holding the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adult content is material restricted to grown-ups, as an X certificate once marked films.

explanation.surface: Raise a drink over a slice from the grill.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink a toast is to raise glasses in honour of someone; toast is also bread browned under heat.

clue.text: Head for drinker with female US writer

parts.note: Philip Roth was an American novelist

explanation.surface: A woman joins an American author at the bar to lead the drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The foamy layer on top of a beer is its head, the bubbles a drinker sees first.

clue.text: Remove listening devices from ruffled budgie I left

indicators.note: ruffled means disturbed, like feathers, so the bird's letters are jumbled
left means departed, so the single letter is taken out of the bird

explanation.surface: Sweep for bugs after a flustered pet bird has flown off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' removes I from BUDGIE, giving BUDGE, and 'ruffled' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a room of hidden microphones, or bugs, is to strip it of surveillance equipment.

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
to rake leaves is to tidy up a garden

explanation.surface: A clergyman is sent to clear up a small wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake is an old word for a thicket or clump of bushes, a small wood.

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written as O
to pen is to write
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A romantic sets out to compose a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air describes something held outdoors rather than under a roof.

clue.text: Cream of society entering the literati

indicators.note: entering says the answer has gone into the words that follow

explanation.surface: The best people join the intellectual set.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the select top layer of a group, its finest members.

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or shady, signalling the letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: Military chiefs might be crooked traders.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaders are people in charge who direct others.

clue.text: I'd join one returning to fool

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the little word next to it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to join a returning friend in deceiving a dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, a nitwit.

indicators.note: interior says the answer lies inside the words given

explanation.surface: Someone confuses old Nyasaland with the hinterland of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Nyasaland (now Malawi) suggests an African country, which is apt misdirection: the answer is another African country spanning the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenya is an East African nation.

explanation.surface: A beverage is ordered for a tennis star.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Perry was a British tennis champion; perry is also a pear cider.
explanation.definitionFit: Perry is an alcoholic drink made from fermented pears; Fred Perry won Wimbledon three times.
